evidence_and_scope.trigger: Docker backend startup on a fresh MySQL volume
observed_errors: Migration MakeTransactionsReceiptIdNullable20260901101931 failed because table transactions does not exist.
MySQL rejected FK_3e8568527418a0d71b12031870c because Goals.category_id and categories.category_id have incompatible signedness.
confirmed_root_cause: TypeORM runs migrations with synchronize=false, but the migration chain has no initial migration that creates users, categories, accounts, transactions, and Bills before alter/index migrations execute.
Category.category_id is currently mapped as signed INT while Goal.category_id is mapped as INT UNSIGNED.
Other current user/category foreign-key properties also mix signed and unsigned INT metadata and would fail or drift after the first reported constraint is corrected.
evidence_and_scope.required_change: Add one earlier idempotent core-schema initialization migration and align foreign-key column signedness with the referenced primary keys. Keep existing later migrations responsible for account uniqueness, username nullability, receipt nullability, and Goals creation/nullability.
out_of_scope: No change to Business Rule semantics, ownership, public endpoints, response envelopes, or UI behavior
No Docker volume deletion, data reset, backfill, or destructive migration
No table rename; established Bills and Goals names remain unchanged
No new domain table beyond the entities already registered by the application

initialization_migration.name: 1700000000000-create-core-tables-if-missing.ts
initialization_migration.ordering: Timestamp 1700000000000 sorts before the existing 1788495106545 account-index migration and all 2026 alter/create migrations.

users: id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY
username VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE before the existing nullable-username migration
categories: category_id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY
transactions: receipt_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL before the existing nullable-receipt migration

entity_alignment.reason: Match Goal.categoryId and Transaction.categoryId foreign keys.
Match the previously approved UC-04 physical schema; public DTO mappings continue to expose nullable string receipt identifiers as required by API contracts.

relationships: accounts.user_id -> users.id with matching INT UNSIGNED types
transactions.account_id -> accounts.account_id with matching signed INT types
transactions.category_id -> categories.category_id with matching INT UNSIGNED types
Bills.user_id -> users.id with matching INT UNSIGNED types
Goals.user_id -> users.id and Goals.category_id -> categories.category_id remain as defined by the previously approved UC-14 migration

sensitive_data_and_exposure.password_storage: password_hash remains bcrypt output in CHAR(60); no password values are placed in migration or logs.
sensitive_data_and_exposure.account_number: account_number_full remains persisted as already modeled; no values are logged or seeded.
sensitive_data_and_exposure.api_contract: No request or response shape changes. Receipt identifiers are explicitly converted at DTO boundaries when non-null.

forward_operations: Create each missing core table in dependency order: users, categories, accounts, transactions, Bills.
Use explicit MySQL types and named foreign keys with matching signedness.
Allow existing later migrations to apply their already-approved changes in order.
migration_plan.rollback: Drop only tables created by this migration and only after confirming all are empty; refuse rollback when any created table contains rows. Drop in reverse dependency order.
migration_plan.data_loss_risk: Forward migration creates only missing tables and does not rewrite or delete rows. Rollback is guarded against non-empty tables.
migration_plan.deployment_considerations: The requested verification uses a fresh empty volume. If an existing volume contains a partial or type-incompatible schema, stop for a separate inspection rather than coercing or dropping it.

assumptions: The target verification volume is empty, as stated by the researcher.

The previously approved UC-04 INT UNSIGNED nullable receipt_id schema remains authoritative for persistence, while API response contracts continue to serialize a non-null receipt identifier as a string.
The previously approved UC-14 Goals creation migration remains authoritative and will run after core categories/users tables exist.
No cascade delete behavior is introduced; existing relationship semantics are preserved.

approval.scope: The exact UC-07 schema proposal recorded in this artifact.
approval.evidence: Researcher statement: I explicitly approve the exact UC-07 schema proposal. Proceed to implement and verify repair-005.
